_comment: LLM-MAINTAINED MODULE MAP. This file is the single source of truth for module boundaries; dependency-cruiser.cjs turns it into lint rules mechanically — never hand-edit the generated rules, edit this map. Refresh it whenever the folder structure changes (see the setup-module-boundaries skill). Every `path` and `publicEntry` is an anchored regex over repo-relative POSIX paths.

modules.name: example-core
modules.comment: A leaf module. Others may import it ONLY through its barrel; its internal files are private.

modules.name: example-feature
modules.comment: A module with more than one public file — list each as a publicEntry.

layers._comment: OPTIONAL directional rules, off unless populated. Each entry forbids the named module from importing the listed modules AT ALL (stricter than public-entry-only). Use for one-directional layering, e.g. a renderer that must never reach the main process.

placement._comment: WHERE FILES MAY LIVE, as opposed to what they may import. dependency-cruiser sees EDGES only, so a module's own file parked at that module's root passes every boundary rule while sitting in the wrong folder — its imports are all legal. These blocks compile into the placement gates (root-files-check.mjs, kind-folder-check.mjs, earned-shared-check.mjs). Each exemption is labelled KIND (the rule does not apply to that category; permanent) or RATCHET (debt; the list may only shrink).

rootFiles.comment: What may sit LOOSE at each module's root. ONE ENTRY PER MODULE IS REQUIRED — a module in `modules` with no entry here FAILS the gate rather than passing unguarded. That inversion is the point: the predecessor gate guarded one hardcoded path, so every module added after it was silently exempt and flattened. A module with nothing to declare writes `{"allow": {}, "ratchet": {}}` and takes two seconds. `path` overrides the root pattern derived from the module's own `path`, and is needed only where the two differ (a module at `src/renderer/` whose root is `src/renderer/src/`). Keys are basenames; values are the reason.

allow.index.ts: KIND — the module's declared public entry. Every module's root holds exactly this by definition.

ratchet.legacyHelper.ts: RATCHET — pre-existing; belongs in the sub-domain that calls it. Delete this entry in the commit that moves the file — the gate fails on an entry naming no file, which is what makes 'the list may only shrink' arithmetic.

example-feature.comment: Every publicEntry that sits AT the module root must appear here — the gate counts files, and a front door is a file. A module whose entry lives one level down (components/index.ts) declares an empty allow instead: nothing legitimately sits loose at its root.

allow.index.ts: KIND — the module's declared public entry.
allow.routes.tsx: KIND — the module's second declared public entry.

kindFolders.comment: Folders named for what files ARE rather than what they are FOR. A kind-folder is the one structural mistake that looks tidy while it spreads. `components/` is deliberately absent: a feature's own `components/` holds one feature's components, which is the opposite of a junk drawer.

earnedShared.comment: A symbol earns the domain-aware shared tier on its THIRD caller, but the gate enforces the FLOOR at two — the house rule calls two callers 'either, copy it or hoist', and arithmetic must not adjudicate a judgement call. Counted per SYMBOL across modules, never per file: everything leaves the tier through a barrel, so a file-level graph shows every module depending on every leaf behind it and proves nothing. `exclude` carries paths earned by CATEGORY rather than by caller count (a vendored primitive kit would stand alone as a published package, so it belongs there from its first caller).
